title: Canada Express Entry 2026: Requirements Guide
metaDescription: Canada Express Entry 2026 explained for Singapore applicants: FSW 67 points, CLB 7 language, CRS up to 1,200, proof of funds and the 60-day ITA deadline.
headline: Canada Express Entry 2026: Eligibility, CRS and Application

sections.title: The three federal programmes
sections.content:
Express Entry manages three federal programmes: the Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Canadian Experience Class and the Federal Skilled Trades Program. Most applicants from abroad come through the Federal Skilled Worker stream, which needs one year of continuous skilled work in a TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3 occupation within the last ten years.

The Canadian Experience Class instead requires one year of skilled work inside Canada in the last three years, while the trades stream needs a valid job offer or a certificate of qualification. Each stream has its own language and education rules, so checking the right stream first saves wasted effort.

sections.title: Language, education and the CRS
sections.content:
Federal Skilled Worker applicants need at least CLB 7 in all four language abilities and must score 67 points on the separate selection grid, which is different from the CRS score. Foreign education needs an Educational Credential Assessment, and proof of funds is required unless the applicant is exempt.

Once in the pool, candidates are ranked by the Comprehensive Ranking System out of 1,200 points, based on age, education, language, experience and extra factors such as a provincial nomination worth 600 points. Draw cut-offs vary by draw type, with category draws for healthcare, STEM, trades and French speakers often lower than general draws.

sections.title: From invitation to permanent residence
sections.content:
When a candidate's CRS score meets a draw cut-off, they receive an Invitation to Apply and have 60 days to submit a complete permanent residence application with police certificates, medical results and supporting documents. Missing documents or errors at this stage can lead to refusal.

Processing for many complete applications takes around six to eight months, though times vary. Applicants already in Singapore should plan language tests, credential assessment and fund documents early, because these steps often take longer than expected.

faqs.q: What is the minimum language level for Express Entry?
faqs.a: Federal Skilled Worker applicants need at least CLB 7 in English or French in all four abilities: reading, writing, listening and speaking. Accepted English tests include IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General and PTE Core, while French applicants use TEF Canada or TCF Canada. Note that IELTS Academic is not accepted for Express Entry.

faqs.q: Do I need a job offer to enter the pool?
faqs.a: No, a job offer is not required to enter the Express Entry pool under the Federal Skilled Worker or Canadian Experience Class streams. A qualifying job offer can add CRS points in some cases, but it is not a precondition. The Federal Skilled Trades stream is different, since it requires a valid job offer or a certificate of qualification.

faqs.q: How does the CRS score work?
faqs.a: The Comprehensive Ranking System scores candidates out of 1,200 points across core human capital, spouse factors, skill transferability and additional points. Age, education, language results and work experience carry the most weight, and a provincial nomination adds 600 points. Higher language scores often add the most points for applicants who can still improve them.

faqs.q: How long do I have after receiving an invitation?
faqs.a: After receiving an Invitation to Apply, you have 60 days to submit a complete permanent residence application. That deadline is strict, so police certificates, medical exams, proof of funds and work references should be prepared before entering the pool where possible, rather than after an invitation arrives.
